decision: Activate the already selected one-thread child-panic regression only after committing its immutable source, runtime, configuration, matrix and inert-controller bindings. It remains the highest-value feasible item because it can retire a specifically identified one-worker operational uncertainty using existing bytes. Pipeline completeness remains broader but cannot start before its independent checked-object receipt-semantics protocol gate is met.

categories.assessment: The active item is a finite conformance regression with a direct parent-versus-worker diagnostic comparison. Pipeline completeness remains a broader discovery method but is not yet protocol-ready.

The one-worker panic-observation boundary is a narrow unresolved operational asset that can be settled by two controls and two candidate cells. A checked-object receipt sentinel could later be shared more broadly, once its input semantics are frozen.
Neither candidate has present evidence requiring an external action. The active regression remains local-only and reports infrastructure or control failure without asserting an upstream defect.

The active item reuses the pinned source, existing mutation and existing control/candidate bytes rather than introducing a new input. Pipeline completeness still needs its own producer, adapter and receipt-semantics review before reuse can be justified.

The active four-cell protocol directly removes the last fixed one-thread diagnostic uncertainty and has a committed prelaunch gate. Pipeline completeness is blocked locally by a scientific protocol gate, not by an external dependency.

candidates.rationale: ACTIVE after its exact prelaunch package was bound. The four existing-byte cells, two offline builds, 30-second process cap, sampled-RSS supervision and raw diagnostic predicates are all finite; its own committed launch gate still prevents any process before the entry checkpoint is delivered.

This remains the strongest alternative with broader transferable value, but its producer, adapters, checked-object receipt semantics, independent expected contents and fault rubric are not yet bound in a finite protocol.

blockers.reason: Bind the supported producer and adapters, a twelve-declaration expectation, receipt semantics, fixed faults and finite source/setup/build/tooling/process controls before promotion.
